title: How to Water Indoor Plants Without a Fixed Schedule
summary: Use the plant, pot, soil and season to decide when to water instead of following a calendar.
body:
A watering routine is useful, but the same interval will not suit every plant. Pot size, drainage, light, temperature and the plant's growth all affect how quickly its growing medium dries.

Check before watering. Feel the top layer of the mix, and learn the usual weight of the pot when it is dry and after it has been watered. A moisture meter can help, but use it alongside the plant's condition rather than as the only signal.

When the plant needs water, water the growing medium evenly until a little drains from the bottom. Empty the saucer so roots are not left standing in water. If the soil is still damp, wait and check again later.

Adjust through the year. Warm, bright or breezy conditions can dry pots faster; cool or low-light conditions can slow them down. If leaves yellow or droop, check the soil and drainage before adding more water, because both dryness and waterlogged roots can cause similar signs.

title: Plan a Balcony Garden Around Light and Drainage
summary: A simple way to choose balcony plants by observing sunlight, wind, space and safe water runoff.
body:
Spend a day noticing how sunlight moves across the balcony. Record where direct sun falls in the morning and afternoon, and which areas stay bright without direct sun. Choose plants whose light needs match those places.

Check wind and heat as well as light. A high or exposed balcony may dry pots quickly, while a sheltered corner can stay humid. Group plants with similar needs, but leave enough space for airflow and for you to water and inspect them.

Use stable containers with drainage holes. Place saucers or trays where they will not overflow onto neighbours or building surfaces, and empty standing water when needed. Select a pot size suited to the plant's roots; a very large pot can hold moisture for longer than a small plant can use.

Start with a few plants and observe how they respond before expanding. Keep notes about the light and how quickly each pot dries. Those observations are more useful than a fixed watering timetable when the weather changes.

title: Monsoon Care for Potted Plants
summary: Protect container plants during rainy, humid weather by checking drainage, airflow and soil moisture.
body:
Rain can keep potting mix wet for longer than usual. Check the soil before watering and pause routine watering when the mix is still damp. Make sure drainage holes are open and move pots out of places where water collects.

Give leaves and stems room to dry. Avoid crowding pots together, remove fallen or damaged leaves, and improve airflow where practical. If a plant is in a sheltered spot, continue checking its soil because it may receive less rain than nearby pots.

Inspect plants regularly for soft, darkened stems, persistent leaf spots or pests hiding under leaves. These signs can have several causes, so first check moisture, light and airflow. Remove only clearly damaged material with clean tools.

When heavy rain is forecast, secure light containers and protect plants that are not suited to prolonged wet conditions. Local monsoon patterns vary, so use the plant's needs and the actual conditions on your balcony or in your garden as your guide.
